text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on August 6 in history:
1600 - Henry IV of France invaded Savoy after negotiations broke down over Saluzzo, controlled by Savoy since 1588.
1623 - Anne Hathaway, wife of English dramatist and poet William Shakespeare, died.

1660 - Diego Velazquez, Spanish painter, died. He became a major figure of 17th century art and was famed for his realism. Among his most famous works are "Las Maninas" (Maids of Honour) and "Venus and Cupid".
1726 - Russia became part of the Treaty of Vienna (signed 1725) and put 30,000 troops at the disposal of her allies in return for support against a possible war with the Ottoman Empire.

1775 - Irish leader Daniel O'Connell born. He was known as "the Liberator". Unable to take his seat after his overwhelming election victory in 1828 in County Clare, he forced the British government to accept Roman Catholics in parliament by the passage of the Emancipation Act of 1829.
1806 - The Holy Roman Empire ended when Francis II renounced the crown and became Francis I Emperor of Austria.
1809 - Alfred, Lord Tennyson, English poet, born. English poet laureate, he was best known for "The Lady of Shallott" and "The Charge of the Light Brigade".
1824 - In the Peruvian War of Independence Colombian patriots with Simon Bolivar defeated the Spanish at the battle of Junin north west of Lima.
1825 - Bolivia was proclaimed an independent republic after nearly 300 years of Spanish rule.
1881 - Sir Alexander Fleming, Scottish bacteriologist who discovered penicillin (1928), born. He won the Nobel Prize for medicine (1945) with Howard Florey and Ernest Chain.
1890 - Convicted murderer William Kemmler became the first human to die in an electric chair at Auburn Prison, New York.
1896 - French parliament voted for the annexation of Madagascar.
1911 - Lucille Ball, U.S. actress and comedienne, born. In films from 1933, she was famous for her television appearances in "I Love Lucy".
1914 - In World War One Austria-Hungary declared war on Russia and Serbia declared war on Germany.
1915 - Fresh allied landings of 25,000 men on Suvla Bay on the Gallipoli Peninsula failed; 252,000 allied troops were casualties of the Gallipoli campaign between 1915-1916.

1916 - Dom Mintoff, Maltese politician, born. A firebrand prime minister, he led his country from 1971 and steered Malta away from its traditional links with Britain and Europe and closer to Libya and the Arab world.
1917 - Robert Mitchum, U.S. film actor, born. In films from 1943, he was best known for his roles in "Night of the Hunter", "Ryan's Daughter" and "Farewell My Lovely".
1918 - In World War One the second battle of the Marne ended. In what was the last German attack on the Western Front they suffered at least 100,000 casualties.
1926 - U.S. swimmer Gertrude Ederle became the first woman to swim the English Channel. The swim took just over 14 hours.
1928 - Andy Warhol, U.S. artist and a pioneer of pop art, born.
1940 - Estonia formally absorbed into the Soviet Union as the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic.

1945 - U.S. air force dropped the first atomic bomb on Hiroshima, Japan. It was carried by the B-29 bomber "Enola Gay". Five square miles (13 sq km) were reduced to ashes and at least 117,000 people were killed.
1962 - Jamaica became independent after 300 years of British rule
1973 - Fulgencio Batista y Zaldivar, Cuban dictator from 1952-59. died. He fled Cuba after being toppled by Fidel Castro.

1978 - Pope Paul VI, who succeeded John XXIII as pope in 1963, died. A conservative, he re-affirmed the Catholic Church's prohibition of birth control in his encyclical "Humanae Vitae". He was succeeded by John Paul I.
1981 - A coup bid against President Jarawa of Gambia ended when British SAS troops helped Senegalese troops to free some 30 hostages still held by rebels.
1990 - U.N. Security Council voted 13-0 to ban trade with Iraq except for medicine and some food for humanitarian relief after the Iraqi invasion of Kuwait.
1996 - U.S. scientists revealed they had found evidence of ancient life on Mars in remnants of a meteorite discovered in Antarctica.
